title: 1951_Mokotów_Prison_execution
text: All executed were members of WiN , who during World War II took active part in anti-Nazi resistance .	World War II	World War II

title: 1951_Mokotów_Prison_execution
text: The executed men were : Łukasz Ciepliński , Karol Chmiel , Adam Lazarowicz , Józef Rzepka , Józef Batory , Mieczysław Kawalec and Franciszek Błażej . title: 1951_Mokotów_Prison_execution
text: All of the men were apprehended in late 1947 and early 1948 , and almost all came from the Rzeszów area .	Rzeszów	Rzeszów

title: 1951_Mokotów_Prison_execution
text: They were personally chosen to take part in anti-communist resistance by Ciepliński , commanding officer of the WiN 's 4th Headquarters , who chose them because of their moral fortitude and their unbroken spirits .

title: 1951_Mokotów_Prison_execution
text: The interrogations conducted by Communist investigators that ensued were particularly brutal .

title: 1951_Mokotów_Prison_execution
text: All seven were tortured and severely beaten ; Cieplinski 's legs and hands were broken , and he had to be carried for meals in a blanket .

title: 1951_Mokotów_Prison_execution
text: A staged trial that took place on October 5 , 1950 , was led by a group of ruthless military prosecutors from the Warsaw Military District - Colonel Aleksander Warecki -LRB- real name Warenhaupt , who served as the presiding judge -RRB- , Major Zbigniew Furtak , Major Zbigniew Trylinski and Lt. Col. Jerzy Tramer , who served as the Public Prosecutor .	Warsaw	Warsaw	Aleksander Warecki	Aleksander Warecki	Zbigniew Furtak	Zbigniew Furtak	Zbigniew Trylinski	Zbigniew Trylinski	Jerzy Tramer	Jerzy Tramer

title: 1951_Mokotów_Prison_execution
text: The accused were not given an opportunity to refute charges brought against them , despite the fact that on several occasions Ciepliński had stated that he was tortured and that his confessions were extracted with the use of torture .

title: 1951_Mokotów_Prison_execution
text: The Communist judges disregarded his testimony .

title: 1951_Mokotów_Prison_execution
text: The courtroom was filled with UB functionaries .

title: 1951_Mokotów_Prison_execution
text: With approval of the presiding chief judge Warecki , the prosecutors publicly mocked the accused .

title: 1951_Mokotów_Prison_execution
text: The newspaper articles which covered the case ran stories that the accused men were `` Traitors , spies and American servants -LSB- who -RSB- will be prosecuted '' .

title: 1951_Mokotów_Prison_execution
text: The accused accepted their sentences with calmness , as they had anticipated the outcome of the trial to result in their deaths .

title: 1951_Mokotów_Prison_execution
text: With the court ruling of five consecutive death sentences , the first of the seven men to be executed was Łukasz Ciepliński .	Łukasz Ciepliński	Łukasz Ciepliński

title: 1951_Mokotów_Prison_execution
text: Colonel Warecki stated afterwards that all seven were collaborating with Nazi occupiers and had betrayed Poland .

title: 1951_Mokotów_Prison_execution
text: After the trial , the men were moved to the Mokotów Prison , where they spent the next 137 days awaiting their execution .	Mokotów Prison	Mokotów Prison

title: 1951_Mokotów_Prison_execution
text: Appeals for clemency sent to then Communist Poland 's president Bolesław Bierut remained unanswered , and the condemned men prepared themselves for death .	Bolesław Bierut	Bolesław Bierut

title: 1951_Mokotów_Prison_execution
text: Realizing that his tormentors would dispose of his body , Ciepliński decided to swallow a small portrait of the Virgin Mary , which he had worn on his neck .

title: 1951_Mokotów_Prison_execution
text: During this time , the condemned men shared the same large cell with other 80 anti-Communist fighters , among them Zygmunt Szendzielarz .	Zygmunt Szendzielarz	Zygmunt Szendzielarz

title: 1951_Mokotów_Prison_execution
text: According to the surviving witnesses , the WiN members supported and helped each other , tending particularly to Ciepliński and Błażej , both of whom suffered the most during brutal interrogations .

title: 1951_Mokotów_Prison_execution
text: In the letter to his wife Jadwiga smuggled out of the prison shortly before his death , Ciepliński wrote :

title: 1951_Mokotów_Prison_execution
text: `` My time is near .

title: 1951_Mokotów_Prison_execution
text: When they will be leading me out of my cell to die , my last words to my friends will be : I am happy that I will be murdered as a Catholic for my faith , as a Pole for my country , and as a human being -LSB- I will die -RSB- for justice and truth -LSB- ... -RSB- My last farewell will be only to you .

title: 1951_Mokotów_Prison_execution
text: I believe that the Holy Mother will take my soul -LSB- ... -RSB- and I will continue to serve Her and report to her about the tragedy of the Polish Nation - murdered by one -LSB- nation -RSB- and abandoned by the others . ''

title: 1951_Mokotów_Prison_execution
text: Shortly before the execution , which took place in the old boiler-room of the prison , Karol Chmiel tried to escape by running along the courtyard and screaming `` They are murdering us . ''	Karol Chmiel	Karol Chmiel

title: 1951_Mokotów_Prison_execution
text: He was captured on a pile of coal .

title: 1951_Mokotów_Prison_execution
text: Even though he had been promised that his letters would be mailed to his sons ; the promise was never kept .

title: 1951_Mokotów_Prison_execution
text: All seven men were shot on March 1 , 1951 , at five - to ten-minute intervals .

title: 1951_Mokotów_Prison_execution
text: They were executed with a single shot to the back of the head , the standard Communist execution method and consistent with the executions at Katyn Forest .	Katyn Forest	Katyn Forest

title: 1951_Mokotów_Prison_execution
text: The executions began at approximately 8 p.m. , with Ciepliński being shot first , followed by Batory at 8:05 , Chmiel at 8:15 , Kawalec at 8:20 , Lazarowicz at 8:25 , Blazej at 8:35 , and Rzepka at 8:45 .

title: 1951_Mokotów_Prison_execution
